title: Scope/port discipline — refuse bare-host targets without explicit port or network-scope flag
goal: Block the failure mode where a scope entry of bare `127.0.0.1` (or any bare hostname/IP without scheme+port) silently fans out into a full local-services scan when nmap-class runners pick it up. Reproduced live 2026-05-20: target-intel normalized `127.0.0.1` to `https://127.0.0.1` (web — safe) but the same scope value, when consumed by nmap with default `--top-ports 100`, would scan 100 local services (Postgres 5432, the AegisPT API itself, dev daemons). This is a scope-leakage class bug, not a capability gap.
scope: Pure additive guard (no behavior change in normal flow): (1) new `api/app/services/scope_validator.py` `validate_target_scope(value: str, *, kind: str) -> ValidationResult` that rejects bare host/IP unless kind=='network' OR an explicit `--scope-mode=network` engagement flag is set. (2) called from engagement create + scope-update endpoints (where targets enter the system) — single line per endpoint. (3) unit tests covering: bare host rejected for kind=url, bare host accepted for kind=network, scheme+port accepted, network-mode escape hatch accepted. (4) docs/security/scope-port-discipline.md explaining the rule + why + the escape hatch.
generation_reason: Operator-flagged 2026-05-20 during backlog-407 live smoke: 'target-intel running 127.0.0.1 — kan toch niet zonder poort nummer aangezien je dan de complete machine lokaal scant?' Investigation showed target-intel itself is HTTP-only (safe), but the same scope value propagates unchecked to nmap which DOES scan many local ports by default. Per ANTI_DRIFT Rule 1: this is a safety-gate task, not a capability task — delta-metric is 'bare-host scope writes rejected at API boundary'.

constraints.active_task_gate: Do not implement until this package is the single active task in NEXT_TASK.md AND ANTI_DRIFT.md + SESSION_PROMPT.md have been loaded.
constraints.scope_creep_guard: Validator added ONLY at API ingestion boundaries (engagement create + scope update). Do NOT add runtime checks inside runners — runners must remain dumb tools.
constraints.no_capability_drift: This task adds NO scanning capability. Per ANTI_DRIFT Rule 1: it BLOCKS a leakage path, not enables a new one.
constraints.must_have_escape_hatch: Operators doing legitimate internal network assessments MUST be able to set scope kind=network OR engagement flag scope_mode=network to bypass the bare-host rule — documented in docs/security/scope-port-discipline.md.

success_criteria: Metric: bare-host scope writes (kind=url, no scheme+port) rejected with 400 + clear error message at engagement-create and scope-update endpoints.
Metric: escape hatch documented and tested — kind=network OR engagement.scope_mode=network accepts bare host.
Live: attempting to register `127.0.0.1` as kind=url returns 400 with explanation; attempting same as kind=network succeeds.
Greppable: `git grep validate_target_scope` shows ≥2 call sites (engagement create + scope update).
Unit tests cover all 4 cases above.
must_not_touch: Any runner runner.py file (runners stay dumb)
Existing scope storage schema (additive validation only)

acceptance_criteria: Live: POST /engagements with bare 127.0.0.1 (kind=url) returns 400 with message naming the missing port/scheme.
Live: same POST with kind=network succeeds.
Live: same POST with http://127.0.0.1:8080 (kind=url) succeeds.
ZERO changes outside listed key_files (verified via git diff --stat).
